September 11, 2026

Houthis seize Yemen's Red Sea coast and threaten Bab al-Mandeb

tags: war, markets, politics
sources: @aaronparnas, @hunteralexanderhowell

Iranian-backed Houthi forces have completed a rapid takeover of Yemen's Red Sea coastline, including Perim Island, bringing them close to effective control of the Bab al-Mandeb Strait, a chokepoint for oil shipments comparable to the Strait of Hormuz. The advance followed strikes on Saudi Arabia, including a reported hit on the kingdom's east-west crude oil pipeline. According to Axios, Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman personally urged Donald Trump to begin striking the Houthis, and Trump declined. Analysts quoted warn that simultaneous pressure on both straits could constrict oil flows and push prices sharply higher.

Trump promises $5,000 checks if Republicans win the midterms

tags: politics, economy
sources: @aaronparnas, @hunteralexanderhowell, @carolinegleich, @oafnation_actual

Trump said he would give every adult American citizen $5,000 if Republicans win in November, and told CBS he does not believe he needs congressional approval to do it. The nonpartisan Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget estimates the plan would cost more than $1.2 trillion and more than double the federal deficit. Critics noted a 2012 post in which Trump warned against Obama "buying the election by handing out unlimited free money," and pointed to earlier unfulfilled promises of DOGE savings checks and $2,000 tariff rebates. Some former prosecutors have said the offer resembles vote buying, a federal crime carrying a fine and up to two years in prison, while Utah's Republican delegation, which has campaigned on fiscal restraint, has not commented.

Calls to shoot Democrats and a loyalty pledge mark Republican midterm convention

tags: politics, media
sources: @aaronparnas, @hunteralexanderhowell, @total.hypocrisy

At the Republican midterm convention in Dallas, an audience member was audible on the broadcast shouting "he should be shot" as Senator Ted Cruz named Democratic figures including Zohran Mamdani, Abdul El-Sayed and James Talarico. Trump later asked the crowd to raise their right hands and recite a pledge to "the greatest president in the history of the United States," and told supporters they should cheat if necessary because the other side does, without offering evidence. Trump also lunged at and shouted at a reporter while leaving the event, and images showed empty seats in the hall.

Trump-installed prosecutor resigns over lack of evidence in conspiracy probe

tags: legal, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Joe diGenova, a former U.S. attorney installed by Trump in Florida to investigate an alleged conspiracy against the president, has resigned, ABC News confirmed. In remarks to the New York Post, diGenova said that seeking indictments where there is no evidence presents an ethical problem, naming Trump and Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche. The statement would likely be used by defence lawyers should any indictments against Trump's political opponents be brought in Florida.

Anthropic says it blocked attempts to use its AI for bioweapons research

tags: tech, health, defence
sources: @aaronparnas

Anthropic published a threat assessment covering December 2025 to August 2026 saying it halted multiple attempts to use its Claude models for biological weapons research, because it could not determine whether the work encountered was legitimate or malicious. One case study describes a scientist in May 2026 seeking help drafting a grant application for gain-of-function research on the chikungunya virus, to be conducted at a military research institute. The report also documents Russian media outlets using the model to generate online propaganda presented as independent reporting, and attempts to develop conventional weapons including firearms, missiles, armed drones and bombs.

Musk super PAC promotes voter registration site that checks its own list

tags: politics, privacy
sources: @carolinegleich

Elon Musk's America PAC is running a site called Vote Safe that presents itself as a voter registration check but is not a government or non-profit service. It collects names, dates of birth, home addresses, email, phone and location data and tracks page views and clicks, and its privacy policy, rewritten last month according to Judd Legum at Popular Information, permits sharing or selling that data along with inferred traits described as psychological trends, predispositions, attitudes, intelligence and aptitude. Because registration status is checked against America PAC's own voter list rather than official state records, the answers it returns can be wrong. The PAC has spent more than $180,000 in a single week promoting the site on Facebook and Instagram.

Kash Patel directed FBI staff to run a social media influence campaign

tags: politics, media, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

Text messages reported by national security journalist Seth Hettena show FBI Director Kash Patel instructing Ben Williamson, the bureau's head of public affairs, to find accounts posting critical messages about him and about Jeffrey Epstein and to reply to them repeatedly. Patel forwarded a specific post mocking his approval rating and told staff to "find them and post our record" back at them continuously. Williamson responded that one of the targeted accounts was an "Epstein didn't kill himself" account and tried to explain why engaging would look bad, with Patel replying that it was "not about them, it's about the number."

Iran resumes ballistic missile production months after Pentagon declared program destroyed

tags: war, defence, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

Iran is again building ballistic missiles, months after the Pentagon said its missile program had been "functionally destroyed." Separately, Trump said he has no regret over the war with Iran and predicted the conflict will end "right after the election."

Musk texts claim he used "lasers from space" to elect Trump

tags: politics, tech, media
sources: @aaronparnas

NPR has obtained and authenticated text messages between Elon Musk and Ashley St. Clair in which Musk boasts of having "lasers from space" that he used to elect Donald Trump in 2024, writing that he planned to "unleash the anomaly in the matrix" ahead of the November results. Pressed for clarification, Musk allegedly said he had 10,000 lasers in space, an apparent reference to SpaceX. The messages form part of a forthcoming documentary about Musk by Alex Gibney.

LG smart TVs found scanning home networks and recording audio

tags: privacy, tech
sources: @aaronparnas

An investigation first raised by the YouTube channel Gamers Nexus and since corroborated by Malwarebytes and other outlets found that LG OLED televisions scan local Wi-Fi networks to log other connected devices, record audio through built-in microphones, and track viewing and listening activity. Researchers examining the firmware reported the behaviour continues in standby mode and while the sets are disconnected from the internet. Logged devices included computers, other televisions, thermostats and smart home equipment.

Trump says a "little gear" would stop AI turning against humanity

tags: tech, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Asked in an interview whether adequate guardrails exist to prevent AI systems and robots from turning against humanity, Trump said it would be fine because there would always be something to stop them, referring to "a little gear" that could switch them off. The remark drew widespread criticism online questioning whether such an off-switch would exist for advanced autonomous systems.

Federal judge orders return of father deported without a hearing

tags: immigration, legal
sources: @oafnation_actual

A man detained at the Camp Pendleton gate and deported without a hearing has been ordered returned to the United States by a federal judge. The case turns on the absence of any hearing before removal.

US military strike kills three on suspected drug boat in the Caribbean

tags: defence, legal
sources: @oafnation_actual

A US military strike killed three people aboard a vessel that SOUTHCOM says was involved in narcotics trafficking in the Caribbean.

Delaware court reinstates gun restrictions for most 18-to-20-year-olds

tags: legal, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

A Delaware court has reinstated firearm restrictions covering most residents aged 18 to 20. Active-duty military and National Guard members are exempt from the restrictions.

Khobar Towers veterans win $428.5 million judgment against Iran

tags: legal, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

Veterans of the 1996 Khobar Towers bombing and their families have been awarded a $428.5 million judgment against Iran. VA disability ratings were used in part to determine the damages awarded.

Voice-cloning scams impersonate relatives and public figures

tags: tech, privacy
sources: @aaronparnas

Scammers are using AI-generated voice clones of victims' family members to request money, in one reported case placing a call that appeared to come from a man's wife asking for a credit card to pay for gas while she was in fact at home. Similar calls have impersonated public figures, including one creator whose cloned voice was used to call a follower. Security advice circulating in response includes agreeing on a private safe word with family members.

Fort Hood soldier avoids jail after pleading guilty to felony strangulation

tags: legal
sources: @oafnation_actual

A Fort Hood soldier who pleaded guilty to felony strangulation and admitted assaulting a pregnant soldier received ten years of supervision and no jail time.

82nd Airborne sergeant sentenced for pointing loaded gun at fellow soldier

tags: legal
sources: @oafnation_actual

An 82nd Airborne sergeant who pointed a loaded weapon at a soldier from his own unit and then reported himself was sentenced to five months confinement and a bad-conduct discharge.

Trump appears to close his eyes during Pentagon 9/11 ceremony

tags: politics, media
sources: @aaronparnas

A Getty Images photograph taken by Finn Gomez at the Pentagon's 9/11 memorial ceremony in Washington shows the president with his eyes closed, and footage of the service shows him repeatedly struggling to keep them open. The ceremony followed a late night at the Republican convention in Dallas. Comparisons were drawn to years of Republican attacks on Joe Biden's alertness.
